findings.title: Covering changes from wave to response
findings.claim: The scene begins with a wave covering the passengers and ends with a person who covers the favor through ingratitude. With 31:31 naming favor and signs, the movement shifts covering from an external danger imposed on them to a response they can choose after rescue.
findings.mechanism: The focus covering verb and wave form one physical image; its final ingratitude word carries the supplied favor-covering facet. The preceding favor-and-sign scene independently activates the second use and returns it to the focus's final word.
findings.reader_payoff: The end of the verse answers its opening image: after surviving a cover they could not control, the survivor's conduct can either recognize the favor or cover it.
findings.containment: This is a cross-root synthesis, not a claim that the two words have the same lexicon branch or that every survivor chooses ingratitude. The focus preserves the measured response as well as the betrayer.

epistemic.reason: Both focus branches and the favor/sign context are supplied; the change of agency across the verse is an integrated inference.
